solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Despicable party game

parts.note: base means low, contemptible
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a party game they find contemptible.
explanation.definitionFit: The American bat-and-ball sport played on a diamond is a game.

clue.text: Move to accommodate one bird

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Asking someone to shift so a bird can perch.
explanation.definitionFit: A budgerigar, the small Australian parakeet, is a bird.

clue.text: Bit of a comic set in sleazy venue

parts.note: a comic strip is a short series of panels in a comic
a club is a set or group of people

explanation.surface: A comedian's routine takes place in a seedy nightspot.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub where performers undress is a sleazy venue.

clue.text: Public transporter totally empty, big up top?

parts.note: a bus is public transport

indicators.note: empty means the inside is removed, leaving the outer letters of totally

explanation.surface: An empty bus with a top deck sounds big on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a large bust describes a woman big on top.

clue.text: Small room on seaside structure more absurd

parts.note: the loo, or toilet, is the smallest room
a pier is a walkway built out to sea at a resort

explanation.surface: A toilet on a seaside pier is even sillier.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazier, battier: the comparative of an informal word for mad.

clue.text: Earliest characters, you and I adopting a primitive calculator

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the letter is placed within the characters

parts.note: the first letters of the alphabet are ABC
together you and I are us

explanation.surface: An instruction for building an early counting device from the first letters of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads on wires, the bead frame was an early device for doing sums.

clue.text: Sporting approach putting defenders before attacking player

indicators.note: before means the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: backs are defensive players in football
a wing is a forward on the flank

explanation.surface: A team tactic placing defence ahead of attack.
explanation.definitionFit: The movement drawing back a club or racket before a shot is an approach to striking the ball.

clue.text: Found in Mexico, a tigerish raccoon-like mammal

indicators.note: found in means the letters are sitting inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A striped wild creature living in Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-nosed relative of the raccoon from Central and South America.

clue.text: Nearest rank encapsulating good officer

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing, so one piece holds the other
rank means foul or corrupt, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: The nearest grade includes a good officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks military but signals an anagram of NEAREST, which holds G.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-commissioned officer in the army or police.

clue.text: Number I fathered brought about ridicule

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so the assembled string is read backwards

parts.note: to sire is to father offspring

explanation.surface: A man's paternity claim causes mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' turns NOISIRED round; it looks like 'caused'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridicule and scornful mockery are synonyms.

clue.text: Gut etc, hole for cake

indicators.note: to gut is to remove the insides, leaving only the outer letters of etc

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den or hole

explanation.surface: Reads like a butcher's or cook's list of offal and a hole, ending with a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A choux pastry finger filled with cream and topped with chocolate is a kind of cake.

clue.text: Diet of war charts served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: maps are charts

explanation.surface: War rations and military maps being dished up.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinned spiced ham was a staple ration in the Second World War, so part of the wartime diet.

clue.text: Suggest thickness of one metre?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
ply is a layer or thickness of material

explanation.surface: A query about whether something is a metre thick.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint at something without saying it outright is to suggest it.

clue.text: I head for pantaloons, enormous trousers cool!

indicators.note: used as a verb, trousers means pockets or takes in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: massive means enormous

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of pantaloons

explanation.surface: Someone boasts about their huge baggy pantaloons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like clothing but is a verb: MASSIVE takes in P.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unmoved and showing no emotion is cool in the sense of calm.

clue.text: Black look, piece of coal on fire perhaps?

definitions.text: piece of coal on fire perhaps?
definitions.meaning: cryptically, something that glows, as a burning coal does

explanation.surface: Someone darkly eyes a burning lump of coal.
explanation.definitionFit: An angry scowl is a black look; read as glow plus -er, it is something that glows.

clue.text: Brave accompanying bear

parts.note: with means accompanying
to stand something is to bear it

explanation.surface: A courageous companion for a bear.
explanation.definitionFit: To brave something is to endure or resist it.

clue.text: So I'm swimming, all toes probably wet

indicators.note: letters swimming about are mixed up and rearranged

parts.note: most people have ten toes in all

explanation.surface: A swimmer remarks that all their toes are probably getting wet.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen something is to make it slightly wet.

clue.text: Drink one at a time in irritating manner

parts.note: tea is a drink
singly means one at a time

explanation.surface: Annoyingly sipping a drink individually.
explanation.definitionFit: Done mockingly, in a way that provokes or annoys.

clue.text: A judge wearing shoe — or not?

definitions.text: A judge wearing shoe — or not?

indicators.note: wearing means inside, as a foot is in a shoe

parts.note: a boot is a kind of shoe
a ref, short for referee, judges a game

explanation.surface: A referee who may or may not be wearing footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay pictures a shod referee; 'or not?' turns the whole clue into the definition, someone not wearing a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: With no shoes or socks on the feet.

clue.text: Judge observing a right tooth, say?

parts.note: a tooth is an example of something that bites

explanation.surface: A judge watching a dentist's case concerning a right tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter settles disputes, like a judge or referee.

clue.text: Tend back

definitions.meaning: to tend children is to bring them up, raise them

explanation.surface: Two words with no picture beyond a nurse looking after someone's back.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up young is a verb sense, while hindmost is the other.

clue.text: Flipping keen about dancing ultimately, this music's syncopated

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the letter
flipping means turning over, so the word is reversed

parts.note: eager means keen

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of dancing

explanation.surface: An enthusiast of dancing praises the off-beat rhythm of a music style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' turns EAGER into REGAE, which goes about G.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaican popular music is known for its offbeat, syncopated rhythm.

clue.text: Report again gets the others worried

parts.note: the rest means the others
ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried

explanation.surface: Repeating a report makes the colleagues anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something once more is to say it again.

clue.text: Ivy League university, one briefly showing flag

parts.note: Penn is the University of Pennsylvania

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the word one

explanation.surface: An elite American college waves a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow pointed flag, as flown on a lance or mast.

clue.text: Old people cast runes all over the place

indicators.note: letters scattered all over the place are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ancient folk throwing runes about for divination.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient inhabitants of Etruria in Italy are an old people, a nation of antiquity.

clue.text: Something further to say as cavalryman, possibly?

definitions.meaning: an extra clause or condition added to a statement
a horseman is one who rides

explanation.surface: A horseman might have one more thing to add.
explanation.definitionFit: An added proviso is one sense; a person on horseback is the other.

clue.text: State number one, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word sounds like the answer when spoken

parts.note: main means chief, number one

explanation.surface: A question about which state is the top one.
explanation.definitionFit: The New England state in the far north-east of the USA.

clue.text: Sitter partially fumbled, ominously knocked the wrong way

indicators.note: knocked the wrong way means the letters are turned back to front
partially means only part of the words is used

explanation.surface: A sitter fumbles in an ill-omened way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' takes LEDOM from 'fumbled ominously'; 'knocked the wrong way' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who poses for an artist is a sitter.

clue.text: Somewhere in Greater Manchester meat past its sell-by date?

parts.note: something past its sell-by date is old
ham is a meat

explanation.surface: A dig at stale meat found in a northern English town.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in north-west England that is part of the Greater Manchester county.

clue.text: Top Welsh location

definitions.meaning: a knitted woollen jacket worn on the upper body
a town on the west coast of Wales

explanation.surface: Might read as the best place in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttoned knitted jumper is a top; the same name belongs to a town in Ceredigion, Wales.

clue.text: Strong words reporting attack on Bangkok, perhaps?

indicators.note: reporting signals that the phrase is spoken aloud

parts.note: a raid in Thailand, of which Bangkok is the capital, is a Thai raid

explanation.surface: News coverage of an assault on the Thai capital, using fierce language.
explanation.definitionFit: A long angry speech of denunciation is a stream of strong words.

clue.text: Methodist seen way off, round back of cathedral

indicators.note: round means placed around the letter
off means wrong or unsettled, so the letters are rearranged
the back of a word is its last letter, of cathedral

explanation.surface: A Methodist is seen off by a road near a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of SEEN WAY goes round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of John Wesley, founder of Methodism, are Methodists.
